name: Ksheerarama (Ksheera Ramalingeswara Temple)
deity: The presiding deity is Ksheera Ramalingeswara Swamy, a form of Shiva worshipped as a milk-white lingam. His consort is revered here as Parvati, and the site is also associated with Maha Lakshmi.
summary: Ksheerarama at Palakollu is one of the five Pancharama Kshetras, a group of ancient Shaiva shrines in the Godavari delta of coastal Andhra Pradesh. The temple enshrines Shiva as Ksheera Ramalingeswara Swamy, worshipped in the form of a milk-white lingam. It is known for its towering nine-storey gopuram, among the tallest temple towers in the region.

sections.history: Ksheerarama counts among the oldest living temples of the Godavari region, with traditions tracing its origins to remote antiquity and much of its surviving fabric to the medieval centuries. It is associated with the Eastern Chalukyas and, by tradition, with the ruler remembered as Chalukya Bhima, under whose patronage temple building flourished across this coastal country. Successive dynasties and local patrons are believed to have extended and repaired the complex over the centuries, adding halls, gateways and the great tower that dominates the town today. As one of the Pancharama Kshetras, the shrine has drawn pilgrims for generations, and its long continuity of worship links the present town of Palakollu to a devotional landscape of considerable age.
sections.architecture: The temple is laid out in the Dravidian manner, with a walled enclosure, pillared halls and a sanctum housing the milk-white lingam. Its most celebrated feature is the soaring main gopuram, rising through nine diminishing storeys to a height of roughly 125 feet, which makes it one of the tallest temple towers in the delta and a landmark visible from far across the flat coastal plain. The tower is ornamented with tiers of sculpted figures and moulded plasterwork, stepping upward to a crowning finial. Within the enclosure stand subsidiary shrines and mandapas, and a sacred tank, or pushkarini, is associated with the site, following the customary pattern in which a temple and its water body form a single sacred whole.
sections.legends: In the Pancharama tradition, the five lingams are said to derive from a single great lingam once held by the demon Tarakasura, which shattered into pieces that fell at five places across the Andhra country; Ksheerarama is counted among them. The name Ksheera, meaning milk, is explained through the lingam's milk-white hue and through an association with the ocean of milk of Vaishnava lore, linking the site to Vishnu as well as Shiva. The epithet Ramalingeswara reflects the belief that Sri Rama himself worshipped Shiva at this spot. Together these stories weave the shrine into the wider mythic geography that binds the five Pancharama temples into a single pilgrimage.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri is the principal festival at Ksheerarama, observed with night-long worship and a celebrated Kalyanotsavam, the ceremonial wedding of the deity and his consort, which draws large gatherings to the temple. The month of Karthika, sacred to Shiva, is also marked with special observances and lamp offerings, when devotees visit through the season in significant numbers. As one of the Pancharama Kshetras, the temple sees pilgrims who seek to worship at all five shrines, and festival days lend the town a particular liveliness. Times and arrangements for major festivals can change from year to year, so intending visitors should confirm details locally.
sections.experience: A visit to Ksheerarama begins, for most, with the sight of its great tower rising above the rooftops of Palakollu long before the temple itself comes into view. Within the enclosure the atmosphere is unhurried and devotional, the milk-white lingam at the heart of the sanctum drawing quiet reverence. The sacred tank and pillared halls offer shaded places to pause, and the surrounding delta town, threaded by canals and green with paddy, gives the pilgrimage a gentle coastal character. Mornings and evenings, when worship is most active and the heat least pressing, are the pleasant times to come. Visitors often pair the shrine with the other Pancharama temples, travelling between them across the Godavari country.

visit.timings: The temple generally opens in the early morning and again in the evening for worship, with a midday closure common at temples in the region. Exact hours vary and should be verified locally before travelling.
visit.dressCode: Modest, traditional attire is appropriate; shoulders and knees should be covered, and footwear is removed before entering the temple precincts.
visit.photography: Photography rules vary and may be restricted within the sanctum. Visitors should look for posted notices and ask temple staff before taking photographs.
visit.gettingThere: Palakollu lies in West Godavari district, close to the towns of Bhimavaram and Narasapuram. It is reachable by rail via Palakollu and Bhimavaram stations, and the nearest airports are at Rajahmundry and Vijayawada.
